# CLAIMs with `tags` `agency`

*Topics — What a work is about. Nucleation holds whatever reading the owner files here, whether or not an Anthology of the SOTA topic could also hold it; instruction for ML practice belongs to the anthology (ADR-048). The words are seeded from the clusters the reading-time triage of 2026-09-25 found, and grow by decision.*

**Agency** — what it is to be an agent — goals, action, control and the capacity to act — in organisms, collectives or machines. An agent is not thereby an individual, a self or a person (ADR-024); how an agent's behaviour is integrated is behavioral-integration, and governing oneself by one's own standards is self-governance (group: philosophy).

| [CLAIM-347](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-347.md) v5 | Frustration among an organization's demands is an ordinal fact before it is a quantity: the jointly satisfiable sets of demands form a downward-closed complex whose minimal non-faces are the minimal conflicts, relief is strict enlargement of that complex for the same declared demands, reorganizations that relieve different conflicts are incomparable, and dropping or suppressing a demand is not relief | The owner's correction, U37 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "We can do quite a lot with access to an ordering, even if it doesn't give us a true measure." A37 granted it ("I agree with your correction") and built the acceptance sets, their intersection and the compatibility complex. Corrected here: acceptance conditions sit on attainable outcomes, a demand's form depends on whether it demands improvement or maintenance, and A37's weak-preference sets fail only as representations of improvement demands. The definitional facts are shown in the body, including that every pair of demands can be jointly improvable while the triple is not. The sharp edge: relief compares complexes for the same declared demands, so a reorganization that deletes a demand is not compared at all, and two reorganizations can be incomparable. It is the move [CLAIM-128](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-128.md) and [TERM-043](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-043.md) made for translation, in a new line. | Active |
| [CLAIM-349](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-349.md) v7 | An organization's access to a signal, the signal's authority over action, and action on it are separable, and adaptive regulation keeps the first while making the second conditional on evidence; overcontrol, which buys freedom from harmful acts by cutting access or making inhibition unconditional, is a maladaptive regime and not more control, so flexibility is a context-sensitive property of maintained influence relations, not of how much is inhibited | The owner's idea, U42 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, on A41's line that an organization "could become extremely resistant to internal changes while losing its capacity to learn, correct errors, or act at all": "useful connections to the ACT and DBT frameworks here, which provide us with accounts/ontologies of maladaption and productive flexibility". In A42's form: recognizing a signal, granting it authority and acting on it are three steps; ACT's defusion is a mechanism for [CLAIM-156](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-156.md)'s decoupling; DBT adds bounded stabilization before correction; RO-DBT names overcontrol as maladaptive. The sharp edge: these are analogies from human treatment, the organizational classes are A42's proposals, not diagnoses, and RO-DBT's own evidence is "promising but not definitive". | Active |
| [CLAIM-351](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-351.md) v3 | A zero aggregate gradient does not show that the demands it aggregates are reconciled: with positive weights it holds both when every demand's own gradient vanishes and when nonzero gradients cancel, and in the second case no update improves them all to first order; even the first is only joint first-order stationarity, which a demand's maximum or saddle also has | A33 §5 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "Zero aggregate gradient does not imply absence of frustrated demands." With L₁ = (θ − 1)² and L₂ = (θ + 1)² at θ = 0 ([CASE-115](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-115.md)), the equal-weight gradient is zero and the aggregate is at its global minimum, while each loss is 1 and wants the opposite move. In general a vanishing positive combination of gradients is either every gradient zero or a certificate that no update improves them all, and the scalar cannot tell which. The sharp edge: it is a fact about a weighted sum, not about what a monitor reading it represents. A29's "the unity of the distress signal need not arise from the unity of the underlying causes" is the interpretive reading, kept apart in the body. | Active |
| [CLAIM-352](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-352.md) v6 | Sen's two aspects of freedom divide along the record's line between what an agent can viably reach and the organization that selects among it: viable reachability can stand for the opportunity aspect only through a map from trajectories to valued functionings, which control theory does not supply, and will-organization gives a causal account of part of the process aspect, not of its fairness or legitimacy | The owner's connection, U11 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, quoting A9 and A10 on viable reachability: "This feels reminiscent of ideas from moral philosophy, e.g. Amartya Sen capabilities account." Worked out by A11. Sen's opportunity aspect is what reachability can represent, once a map says which reachable trajectories are valued functionings. His process aspect is in part what will-organization models: whether the agent's own governance selected the outcome. Read first-hand in [NOTE-263](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-263.md) (Sen's lecture) and [NOTE-259](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-259.md) (Robeyns). The sharp edge: reachable states are not capabilities, and an efficacious governance is not a fair or legitimate process. | Active |
| [CLAIM-353](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-353.md) v4 | A will-organization that gives two operators decisive jurisdiction over a pair of options each, respects unanimous preference and admits any profile of operator rankings cannot always choose, and unlike Arrow's impossibility this is not escaped by giving the grant procedure richer, cardinal or comparable, information, so what distributed governance must give up is jurisdiction, unanimity or the domain, not an informational restriction | From U36 of the exchange of 2026-10-17. | [CLAIM-354](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-354.md) v4 | Freedom of will and autonomy come in degrees along several dimensions, among them viable reachability, control cost, robustness to disturbance, governance reconfigurability, revisability and motivational integration, and agents compare by inclusion of what they can viably reach under matched conditions: a partial order with incomparable pairs, not a scalar, and a gradient only of a declared measure | The owner's, U9 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "controllability of a system isn't binary, and neither is sensitivity to perturbation", so can the account speak of "gradations (perhaps even gradients/spectra?) of freedom of will/autonomy". | [CLAIM-356](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-356.md) v6 | An objective that originates outside a learning system can become a goal of the training organization, through its causal role in selecting, stabilizing and reproducing the learned structure it rewards; exogenous origin does not disqualify a goal, but it does not show that the network governs or endorses the objective, and what is selected is performance on the updating distribution, not generalization | The owner's, U35 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, against A34's guardrail that "Loss minimization does not automatically mean the model has its own goals": the externally assigned objective "can motivate identification and persistence of learned features", so the training process can be described as "having endogenous goals". | [CLAIM-357](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-357.md) v9 | The frustration residual and governance regret separate structural infeasibility, realized violation and minimax suboptimality, and identify none of them as thwarting: a positive residual says no admissible update meets every declared requirement, a positive regret only that the actual update's worst residual exceeds the best achievable, which can hold while every requirement is met, and actual violation needs regret above the negative residual; aggregate performance does not tell infeasibility from realized violation, and the multipliers that certify infeasibility need not be the weights governance assigns | A34 §4 and A35 §3.3 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, restated at A39 §2C and A40 §3.4, from A33's "irreducible conflict" and "manufactured frustration". With m(d) the worst residual, Φ its minimum and Γ the actual update's excess over Φ ([CLAIM-365](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-365.md)): Φ > 0 is structural infeasibility; when Φ ≤ 0 the actual update violates a requirement exactly when Γ > −Φ. | [CLAIM-359](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-359.md) v5 | A self-governing organization's robustness to compromised constituents is a property of the processes that allocate, audit and revise authority, not only of its constraints on harmful acts; safeguards against capture can also restrict the disagreement and revision that self-governance needs, and where they do security and self-governance trade off, while others, such as audits independent of the audited that protect dissent, serve both, so the two are distinct achievements and not opposed ones | The owner's question, U41 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "is literature on organizational robustness to insider threats potentially useful to us?" A41's answer, condensed: an insider can aim at the organization's future allocation of authority rather than at the present decision, so robustness must protect the processes that allocate, audit and revise authority, and the same protection can silence the opposition that corrects the organization, though some safeguards protect both. | [CLAIM-361](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-361.md) v4 | Relief of an organization's frustration must be judged for an identified organization against a fixed reference set of its original demands, under an explicit correspondence between earlier and later demands: a demand excised or suppressed has changed the comparison and has not been satisfied, an endogenous revision of what the organization maintains is a transformation of it and not relief, and learning can change which processes bear the demands | The owner's prompt, U38 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, on A37's line that deleting a demand "has changed the comparison problem": "it might be helpful to connect back to our notions of individuation". Worked out by A38 and restated by A39 §2B and A43. | [CLAIM-362](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-362.md) | Non-domination of an agent's subcomponents is a candidate constituent of authenticity as an organizational achievement, not a sufficient criterion of ownership: higher-level processes need not impose the outcome because the lower-level ones already support it or settle their disagreement among themselves, and a process that rarely decides keeps access to the roles in which it is consequential | The owner's, U45 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "'authenticity' should be treated as an organizational achievement characterized by non-domination of subcomponents". | [CLAIM-393](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-393.md) | Ordinary and legal attributions of agency to an artifact cannot serve as the independent marks that would defeat the record's agency test, because they turn on whether its mechanism is understood: a known mechanism invites "This is all just programmed!", an inscrutable one invites fear, whatever the description lengths | From Boyle's "inscrutability paradox" in The Line ([LIT-1288](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1288.md), read in [NOTE-1014](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1014.md)): if an apparently general AI comes from well-understood programming, people will doubt it has autonomous consciousness, since it is "merely doing or saying that which we have programmed it to do"; if its workings are inscrutable, they will find it "more mysterious and potentially more threatening" (p. 30; pp. 54, 246, 272). | [CLAIM-418](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-418.md) v5 | Possessing, enacting or being shaped by an organizational perspective does not establish an independent agent, and perspectival, agential and institutional boundaries need not coincide: several agents can share a perspective, one agent can act through several, and a perspective can be reproduced with no agent governing it; where a perspective contributes to an agent's activity it can enable and constrain the exercise of agency, and that exercise can reproduce or transform it, while whether agency universally requires such a perspective stays open | From the branch of the exchange of 2026-10-22: the owner's question at U38, "what's the relationship between perspective and agency?", A38's answer, and A39's request that it be recorded. | [CLAIM-423](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-423.md) v6 | In a political collective, components that change at different speeds (attention, coalitions, elected terms, administrative careers, law and treaties, generational memory) are not only nested by timescale: under a given institutional arrangement their different temporal horizons affect which forms of influence each can accumulate, exercise and keep, and so which of them holds authority over the others, so a state can stay continuous as an actor while the organization producing its positions changes under it | The owner's, at U28 of the exchange of 2026-10-22: domestic and international politics as the domain where "regime ecology" becomes concrete, with "separation of timescales in elections, durations of tenure in elected and appointed positions, lifespan, generational memory, etc." creating "amorphous collectives of varying orders and degrees of coupling". | [CLAIM-424](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-424.md) v3 | Reflexive governance of an organization's perspectival arrangements, making the conditions that govern its own interpretation, evaluation and action available for effective examination and revision, is a capacity some organizations of perspective have and others lack, not what makes something a perspective; and the capacity to revise those standards is not the capacity to revise them well | A37's definition, from the exchange of 2026-10-22, re-scoping [CLAIM-284](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-284.md). | [CLAIM-430](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-430.md) | An interaction can make available a way of relating that its participants' operative perspectives did not hold, by giving each a role to enact in it, so that taking part can come before, and help produce, the reinterpretation it later seems to express; whether the change stays with the partner, generalizes to a category, or is reproduced beyond the encounter are further questions | From the exchange of 2026-10-22, "Ben Franklin Effect Explained": the owner's U2, asking for Franklin's favour to be read as a "perspectival invitation", and U4, connecting it to intergroup contact. | [CLAIM-482](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-482.md) v2 | An organization's aggregate revealed preference exists exactly when its record of winning moves never cycles, and where it exists it is fitted to one regime of authority, so an intervention on authority that changes the winning moves changes the fitted preference and the preference does not predict the change | The status review of 2026-10-27 ([ADR-057](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-057.md)) found the record's later formal work bearing on an objection it never cited. The thesis's defeated_if is not met: the theorem holds "regardless of ... architecture", makes no matched-resource comparison and no intervention on internals, and its authors say the map runs "from the agent's policy rather than its activations". | [CLAIM-514](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-514.md) | World-modeling is a family of resource-bounded capabilities for producing and using predictions about an environment's possibilities and consequences, each relative to a declared family of questions; a world model in the representational sense is one possible realization of them, competent behaviour can determine environmental structure without identifying any internal mechanism, and producing, maintaining and revising world-modeling capabilities are further achievements, not prerequisites of agency in general | The owner's preferred formulation at the second review of the filing of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31). | [CLAIM-515](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-515.md) v2 | Whether an organization has a cognitive property is four questions, not one: what information about the property can be recovered from its behaviour, what capabilities it can actually exercise, what mechanisms realize them, and whether it can maintain or transform those mechanisms; the four can come apart, and none should be silently substituted for another | The general principle the owner drew at the second review of the filing of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31): "When asking whether an organization 'has' a cognitive property, distinguish the information recoverable from its behavior, the capabilities it can actually exercise, the mechanisms realizing those capabilities, and its ability to maintain or transform those mechanisms." | [CLAIM-519](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-519.md) v2 | Competent behaviour does not establish an internal world model: over a fixed interface and a finite horizon, an agent with no model, whose actions are looked up from the history so far, reproduces the interaction distribution of an agent that has one exactly; a policy can identify predictive structure without any particular internal component realizing it, so compression and generalization support comparing candidate architectures, and establishing an internal mechanism needs evidence that discriminates candidate implementations, such as targeted interventions | The owner's thesis at U20 of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31): that under the record's framework a world model is "essentially a 'folk' explanatory tool and that no such thing need explicitly be present for the external behavior to be indistinguishable from a comparable black box agent which actually did contain a world model". | [CLAIM-523](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-523.md) v9 | For a normatively relevant discrepancy to change what an organization does, three distinct achievements are needed and any can fail while the others hold: legibility, by which the discrepancy becomes recognizable; volitional efficacy, by which a corresponding demand can move action; and correctability, by which a fitting revision can be carried out within deadline and resources; none establishes that the demand or the revision is justified, and whether the norm-satisfying histories the agent can still realize are empty depends partly on what its earlier actions destroyed | The owner's synthesis at review of the filing of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31). | [CLAIM-527](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-527.md) v2 | Viable reach, valence and emotion are three quantities in an organization, not one: an emotion is a claim to precedence, system valence is movement along the ordering that wins the negotiation, and a change in what the organization can viably reach is neither, so an organization can run ahead along its prevailing ordering while its viable reach contracts | Filed 2026-10-31 from the readings of Massumi and McKim (2009) and Bencherki, Brummans and Vézy (2024). | [CLAIM-532](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-532.md) v6 | An unresolved discrepancy is an occasion for self-formation, the transformation dimension of a will-organization, and not a guarantee of it; it suffices for self-formation that the agent's own activity on such a discrepancy produce a maintained capacity, either a new distinction, its policy coming to depend on a feature of its situation it did not depend on, or a new channel, the outcomes it can reach under its own policy growing, that outlasts the discrepancy and serves a class of later ones, as shown by transfer to discrepancies of the same class after the inducing conditions are gone and by interventions on the processes that produce the capacity while it forms | The positive account A33 §7 offered, at the owner's U33 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02), sharpened by the reader of U32–U33 so that it can fail. | [CLAIM-533](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-533.md) v6 | The sensitivity that formal chaos gives a will's dynamics is not control over them: in Kane's self-forming actions, chaotic amplification keeps the outcome open, but it magnifies the agent's efforts, uncontrolled fluctuations and outside inputs alike, so what would make the outcome the agent's is how its own control couples to the amplifying directions, relative to noise and to other parties' inputs and with what feedback, which sensitivity does not supply; and under weak noise what amplification touches lasts only where it reaches the slow modes | The owner's, at U16 and U20 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02). | [CLAIM-535](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-535.md) v5 | An organization that acts on what it observes has a policy acceptable in every circumstance exactly when, for each observation, the circumstances it cannot tell apart share an acceptable action; so every circumstance having an acceptable action does not give a policy, a finer observation never removes one, and where acceptable actions overlap the coarsest observations that suffice are several and incomparable, so which distinctions must be made legible depends on which acceptable action the organization commits to | A33 §4 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02), at the owner's U33 request for positive accounts, with A30 §2's example and A32's Claim B. | [CLAIM-543](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-543.md) v5 | What separates a language model's distribution over personas from a distribution over organizational perspectives is not whether the latent model is hierarchical, since a mixture or an LDA-style admixture already is, but whether some latent components condition which others are available or consequential: a model whose components are exchangeable given their weights is organizationally flat however many levels its prior has, and dependencies among components count as organization (organization as relational arrangement) only where interventions, not fit, support them | The owner's U8 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02): "think of the relations as bayesian hierarchy, so H1 is a flat plate model and H2 has hierarchical/causal structure", said of a language model read as a distribution over perspectives under the Persona Selection Model (U6). | [CLAIM-582](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-582.md) v5 | Under a fixed dynamical model an added hard constraint cannot enlarge the set of admissible trajectories, so it cannot enlarge what some admissible path reaches or lower the least cost of reaching it; what it can improve is a property required of every path a disturbance or a given process may take, such as robustness or reliability, and a constraint that does more has changed the mechanism | A's proposal, from the pasted synthesis on constraint architectures (pasted by the owner on 2026-11-04, continuing the exchange on emergency readiness whose share link could not be fetched): "If K' ⊆ K, then Traj(K') ⊆ Traj(K)". | [CLAIM-1123](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1123.md) | When a driven system feeds back on its drive, the per-switch identity and the summed lower bound of the thermodynamics of prediction still hold, but the nostalgia that bounds the dissipation can be negative, and so can the dissipation and the excess work, so the bound no longer makes nonpredictive memory a cost | [QUESTION-494](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-494.md)'s note asks which conclusions of the passive account survive feedback. [THEORY-026](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-026.md)'s identity, β⟨W_diss⟩ = I[s_t;x_t] − I[s_t;x_{t+1}] per switch, uses no assumption about the drive, and its summed bound needs only that relaxation lowers the nonequilibrium free energy, which a kernel that keeps each equilibrium stationary does whatever chose the signal. Both survive feedback, and the run checks them in 500 random systems. What fails is the sign: once the next signal depends on the state, the state can carry more about x_{t+1} than about x_t, and in the run the summed nostalgia is negative in 323 of 500 systems and the dissipation and excess work in 6. So the bound stops pricing nonpredictive memory and can permit work extraction, paid for by the controller's use of the state, which the source's accounting leaves out. | [CLAIM-1189](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1189.md) | In a percept–action loop, the nostalgia of a memory depends on the policy that uses it and not only on what it keeps: a memory of the context, used to make the action succeed, leaves no trace of itself in the next percept and is wholly nonpredictive, while the same memory left unused can be wholly predictive, and its heat per step is the same either way, so under feedback nostalgia is neither a property of the memory nor its cost | From [CASE-391](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-391.md)'s loop. Percepts are a fresh context u, a sticky nuisance v and the outcome y of the last action, which succeeds when it matches u. A memory that keeps u and acts on it makes every outcome a success, so the next percept says nothing about u: its nostalgia is its whole content, ln 2 per step in the noiseless limit. The same memory with the action fixed lets the outcome reveal u, and its nostalgia is 0. Its heat per step is the same, because the policy only moves dissipation between the switch and the relaxation. Without feedback a memory's nostalgia is fixed by the memory and the drive; with feedback the use that makes the memory worth having is what makes it nonpredictive. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-1199](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1199.md) | The crossed intervention on a small conventionally trained network shows the regulation of conflict shared between the network's learned state and the optimizer, in proportions that the training optimizer sets, so that in conventional training most of that governance does not fall outside the network as a rule | Alternative B. In the run ([CLAIM-1030](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1030.md)) the learned state accounted for 0.58 of the variation in how much of one task the network gave up, against 0.39 for the optimizer, in networks trained by heavy ball; and 0.15 against 0.81 in networks trained by Adam. Where governance sits is then not a fixed fact about conventional training but a result of it: the training optimizer decides how much of the later regulation of conflict the network comes to hold. On this reading the claim's "most" is an overstatement, though its defeat condition is not met. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
